proposed_widenings.name: PolymorphRetainedField additions: class_features, feats, saving_throw_proficiencies
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape retains class features, feats, and saving throw proficiencies — none of which appear in the current PolymorphRetainedField union. Polymorph only needed alignment/personality/creature_type/HP/HD, so the gap didn't surface there.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you retain your creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies

proposed_widenings.name: PolymorphRevertTrigger: incapacitated_condition
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape ends immediately when the druid gains the Incapacitated condition. No current PolymorphRevertTrigger covers a condition-based revert.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You stay in that form [...] until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die.

proposed_widenings.name: PolymorphRevertTrigger: caster_uses_feature_again
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape ends when the druid uses Wild Shape again (auto-revert on re-activation). No current trigger covers 'caster re-activates the same feature'. dismissed_by_caster is the wrong semantics — it is a deliberate early end, not an automatic revert on next use.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You stay in that form [...] until you use Wild Shape again

proposed_widenings.name: PolymorphActionRestriction: no_spells_keep_concentration
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape prevents casting new spells but explicitly preserves ongoing concentration. The existing 'no_speech_no_spells' restriction is wrong on both axes: Wild Shape retains speech ('you retain your [...] ability to speak') and retains concentration ('shape-shifting doesn't break your Concentration').
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can't cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn't break your Concentration or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

proposed_widenings.name: PolymorphFormSource: known_forms_roster
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape draws from a fixed player-curated roster of known forms (4 at L2), not an open 'any Beast of CR ≤ X'. The roster is updated on long rests. The catalog_ref variant with crBound expresses the eligibility constraint but not the roster-of-known-forms restriction. Additionally, the CR cap scales with druid class level (1/4 at L2, 1/2 at L4, 1 at L8), which no existing crBound variant supports.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum Challenge Rating of 1/4 [...] Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.

proposed_widenings.name: DurationValue.amount: LinearPerLevel scaling
proposed_widenings.justification: Wild Shape lasts 'a number of hours equal to half your Druid level'. DurationValue.amount is a bare number; there is no axis-based scaling support parallel to DiceAmount.linear_per_level. The upcastTiers field only handles spell-slot steps, not class-level steps.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level

notes: The structural shape is correct: activation family, Bonus Action cost, use_count resource, partial_short_full_long reset, transform_target effect on self attachment. All gaps are missing variants of existing surface types — nothing requires a new v4 atom. Temp HP = druid level is encodable via a separate grant_temp_hp atom with linear_per_level DiceAmount (axis=class) alongside the transform_target, so tempHpFromForm: true is not needed and is not a gap. The Known Forms scaling table (4/6/8 forms, CR 1/4 / 1/2 / 1, Fly Speed unlock at L8) is class-progression metadata; the crBound scaling gap is the mechanical piece that needs the surface_widening.
